To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mCC10 has a similar 5'-flank region as the rat gene.
the 3.3kb of 5'-upstream sequence of the mouse Clara Cell 16 kiloDalton protein gene contains a cluster of glucorocorticoid response elements, hepatocyte nuclear factors and an Oct1 binding site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of cis acting regulatory elements in the 5'- flanking sequence of the mCC10.
the characterization of the mouse CC10 gene.
the identification of cis acting response elements in the mCC10 promoter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mCC10, rat CC10 and rabbit uteroglobin are members of a multigene family, which have arisen from a common ancestral gene.
the mCC10 and the rat CC10 10 gene 5' regions are highly homologous and share many of the same regulatory elements.
the mCC10 promoter is similar in organization to the rat CC10 promoter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 5'-regulatory region of the mCC10 contains potential cis-acting regulatory elements for the glucorticoid, HNF3 and Oct1 binding proteins and the B1 murine repeat sequence.
the mouse, rat and rabbit CC10 genes have highly similar 5' flanking regions and that the 5' flanked regions contain cis-acting response elements for glucocorticoids, HNF3 and Oct1 binding protein.
the mCC10 and the rat CC10 gene 5'-flank sequences are very similar, however the mCC10 is more homologous to the rabbit uteroglobulin gene sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mouse, rat, rabbit and human CC10 genes have very similar structures.
the 5'-regulatory region of the mouse CC10 gene has a number of cis-acting regulatory elements in common with the 5'-region of the rat CC10 gene, but not with the rabbit uteroglobin gene.
the mouse CC10 promoter is very similar to the rabbit and rat CC10 promoter.
